text:
sven: heads up — saw a sharp GPU queue spike for us-west-2 around 07:58, tail latencies jumped and a handful of requests timed out.

infra-oncall-bot: [ALERT] queue_depth > 80% for gpu-pool-usw2 (3m avg) at 07:59:12 — firing oncall.

lia: yep saw it in the dashboard. spike correlated with a big batch of reranks from customer X and some background eval jobs that started at the same time.

ops-sre: quick snapshot: admission queue hit 92% max, active nodes 42, pending pods 6, node launch LAT median 42s. Not huge but combined with kernel scheduling we hit a shortfall window.

monique: are these cold starts or just transient overload? last time it was cold starts + short scaling lag.

sven: looks like a mix. many requests were for long-context runs => higher token compute per request, so throughput dropped. autoscaler didn't provision enough headroom.

autoscaler-bot: current autoscaler params: scale_margin=0.15, scale_cooldown=45s, smoothing_window=60s, standby_instances=0.

lia: I'd like to try an "elastic headroom" approach instead of increasing standby_instances across the board. Idea: keep small standby in critical regions + bump margin and smoothing window to absorb short spikes.

sven: proposed quick config for canary (us-west-2 only):
```yaml
autoscaler:
  scale_margin: 0.35   # increase headroom to handle 35% transient surge
  smoothing_window: 120s
  scale_cooldown: 30s  # allow faster reaction once trend observed
  standby_instances: 2 # minimal warm capacity to avoid kernel cold penalties
  reserve_credit_seconds: 45s # hold ephemeral headroom for quick bursts
```

ops-sre: cost note: rough estimate = +6-9% hourly GPU usage for that region while canary is on. fine if it's just a controlled canary.

lia: test plan: enable canary 02:00-05:00 UTC (low traffic), run synthetic burst (loadgen) that simulates long-context reranks (12 concurrent 30s requests) x 3 bursts. We'll monitor queue depth, node spinup times, and tail P95 latency.

infra-oncall-bot: ack — scheduled canary window set by @lia for 02:00 UTC. Alert thresholds adjusted: queue_depth > 85% will page.

monique: add a short-runbook step: if node spinups exceed 8 in 3m, revert scale_margin to 0.2 and set standby_instances=0 to avoid cost runaway.

sven: agreed. also let's add a metric to track "burst_hit_rate" (requests that hit queue > 100ms) so we can quantify improvement vs cost.

autoscaler-bot: simulated dry-run on current infra with proposed params shows queue depth peaks reduced by ~48% in 5/10 synthetic runs, median node spinup unchanged.

ops-sre: thumbs up to proceed. owners: @lia (execute canary), @sven (monitor & rollback), @monique (cost guard).

lia: I'll flip the switch and post results after the 02:00 run. Thanks team. :rocket:

sven: one more ask — keep eu-west-1 unchanged for now; similar traffic pattern but capacity tight due to commits. We'll evaluate after succesful USW2 canary.

infra-oncall-bot: closing thread on action items, will reopen if post-canary signals exceed thresholds.
